summary: This article explains why animals become endangered through habitat loss, hunting, and pollution, and how reserves and breeding brought the Arabian oryx back.
introduce: Draw a simple cause → effect arrow on the board and ask students for an everyday example, such as “I did not sleep, so I felt tired.” Tell them that while reading “Why Some Animals Become Endangered” they will find at least two cause-and-effect links.

keyTerms.def: in danger of dying out because very few are left
the natural home of an animal or plant
harmful things, like trash, smoke, or oil, that make land, air, or water dirty

challengeTerms.def: the dying out of every member of a species
to bring a plant or animal back to a place where it used to live
describing a living thing brought to a new place where it spreads and causes harm

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that people can save endangered animals if they work together? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how people can be both a cause of the problem and part of the solution for endangered animals.
struggling: Pre-teach endangered, habitat, and pollution with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers match cause cards to effect cards from the article with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use extinction, reintroduce, and invasive in a short paragraph that explains one important cause-and-effect chain from the article.
